LESSON: PHONOLOGICAL SPEAKING

Grade: Grade 2
Subject: LITERACY ACTIVITIES
Strand: Strand 2
Topic 2.3: Phonological SPEAKING

SECTION 1: WELCOME

• Today’s class: Phonological SPEAKING
• How we learn: Teach → Worked example → Try this
• Use point notes. Show working. Then take the quiz.
• Big question: Which words contain 4 lessons letter-sounds to make  Learners blend syllables to form words and these sounds?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

1. recognize and say multiple groups
2. use appropriate words to games to enable them to listen to different make short, meaningful sounds sentences  Learners give words that rhyme
3. appreciate the role of  Learners are guided to make a list of all the blending and segmenting in sounds they can hear from the forming sentences environment(My home, my community)

SECTION 3: CLASS STUDY (TEACH → EXAMPLE → TRY)

▸ Phonological SPEAKING

• Listen to a model.
• Study the example.
• Then produce your own example.

▸ Phonological SPEAKING

Teach
• Focus skill: recognize and say multiple groups.
• Use complete sentences.
• Speak clearly; write neatly.

Worked example
• Model sentence 1 about Phonological SPEAKING.
• Model sentence 2 using a Kenyan school example.
• Model dialogue: A: “…?”  B: “…”

Try this
• Write 5 original sentences on this skill.
• Say one 30-second oral example to a partner.


SECTION: QUICK EXAMPLES

• One clear model for Phonological SPEAKING
• One Kenyan school/home example

SECTION: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences.
2. Do one oral practice with a partner.
3. Correct spelling/punctuation.

SECTION: WORK TO DO

1. Revision sheet: meaning + 5 examples + 5 practice items.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Which words contain 4 lessons letter-sounds to make  Learners blend syllables to form words and these sounds?

SECTION: REMEMBER

• Model first, then try.
• Use complete sentences.

• Next: complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Classroom study notes (Strategy 2)
